To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dual-plate micro-trench electrodes can be used for voltammetry without added supporting electrolyte, and the resulting currents are stable and reproducible, and that the current response can be controlled by changing the potential of the collector electrode.

the dual-plate gold-gold microtrench electrodes in generator-collector mode can be employed to measure mass transport limited currents at one of the two electrodes without added supporting electrolyte, and that the steady state collector currents remain well-defined and stable in the presence of varying levels of supporting ions.
(i) the generator-collector current response is well-defined and (ii) the steady state collector current is mass transport limited even in the absence/addition of supporting electrolyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the generator-collectorelectrode system in the context of dual-plate gold-gold microtrench electrodes.
the development of a dual-plate micro trench electrode system based on gold-gold electrodes.
the design and characterization of microstructured electrode systems for electrochemical sensing applications.

the microtrench electrodes can be used for generator-collector voltammetry without supporting electrolyte, which is an important feature for sensor applications.
